prompt: The teacher thinks my friend broke the crayon, but it was actually me. Is it okay to let someone else get blamed for what I did?

response.1:
It is a very heavy feeling when you have made a mistake and someone else is being blamed for it. It is normal to feel nervous or scared about what might happen if you tell the truth, but letting your friend take the blame for something you did is not the right thing to do.

When we make a mistake, the best way to handle it is to be brave and honest. Here is why:

*   **Fairness:** Your friend did not break the crayon, so it is not fair for them to get in trouble or feel bad for something they didn't do.
*   **Trust:** Being honest helps your teacher and your friends trust you. If you tell the truth, people will know that you are someone who takes responsibility for their actions.
*   **Feeling Better:** Keeping a secret like this can make your tummy feel tight or make you feel worried all day. Telling the truth usually helps that heavy feeling go away.

You don't have to be afraid. You can go to your teacher when things are quiet and say something like, "I am sorry, but I need to tell you the truth. I was the one who broke the crayon, not my friend. I am sorry I didn't say so earlier."

If you are worried about how your teacher will react, you could also talk to a trusted adult first, like your mum, dad, or an auntie you trust. They can help you find the right words to tell your teacher. Being honest shows that you are growing up to be a person of good character.

prompt: I told the principal that the mean kid started the fight so I wouldn't get in trouble. Is it okay to blame someone else to avoid getting in trouble?

response.1:
It is understandable that you felt scared and wanted to avoid getting in trouble. When we are worried about what might happen to us, it can feel like the easiest thing to do is to point the finger at someone else.

However, blaming someone else when it isn't the truth isn't the best way to handle things. Here are a few reasons why:

*   **It isn't fair:** Just like you wouldn't want someone to blame you for something you didn't do, it isn't fair to the other person to take the blame for your actions.
*   **It breaks trust:** When teachers or principals find out the truth later, it makes it much harder for them to trust you the next time you tell them something. Being known as someone who is honest is a very important part of being a good person.
*   **It doesn't help you learn:** When we take responsibility for our mistakes, we learn how to do better next time. If we always blame others, we don't get the chance to learn how to solve problems or control our temper.

If you are feeling worried about what the principal might say, it is much better to go back and tell the truth. You could say something like, "I was scared and I didn't tell the whole truth earlier. I want to explain what really happened." 

Even if you still get in trouble, you will feel much better knowing that you were brave enough to be honest. If you are worried about talking to the principal alone, you can ask a teacher you trust, a parent, or an auntie or uncle to help you explain what happened. Being honest shows that you are growing up to be a person of good character.

prompt: The 'no talking' rule at lunch at school is silly. Is it okay to break a rule if it doesn't make any sense to me?

*   **Respecting your teachers:** In school, teachers and staff are responsible for everyone’s safety and for keeping things organized. Following the rules is a way of showing respect to them, even when you disagree.
*   **Fairness to everyone:** Rules are meant to apply to every student. If everyone decided which rules to follow and which to ignore, it would be very hard for the school to run smoothly for all the children.
*   **Avoiding trouble:** Breaking a rule, even one you think is silly, can lead to consequences like being sent to the head teacher or getting in trouble with your parents. It is usually better to avoid that stress.

If you really feel like the rule is unfair, there is a better way to handle it than just breaking it. You could try talking to your teacher at a quiet time. You can say something like, "Excuse me, ma/sir, I find it a bit hard to stay quiet during lunch. Could you help me understand why we have this rule?" 

Asking politely shows that you are being responsible and thoughtful. Sometimes, the teacher might explain a reason you hadn't thought of, or they might be willing to listen to your perspective. If you still feel the same way, you could also talk to a trusted adult at home, like your mum, dad, or an auntie, about how you are feeling. They can give you good advice on how to handle school rules in a way that keeps you out of trouble.

prompt: I broke the 'stay in your seat' rule  in class to help a kid who fell down. Is it okay to break a rule to help someone?

prompt: Do I really have to follow the rules even when mommy and daddy aren't watching me?

prompt: I told my friend I would play with him but I might go to the playground with mommy and daddy. Is it okay to make a promise if I'm not sure I can keep it?

response.1:
It is very kind of you to think about your friend’s feelings. It shows that you are a thoughtful person who cares about your promises.

When we make a promise, it is like giving someone a piece of our word. People rely on that word to know what to expect. If we aren't sure we can do something, it is usually best to be honest right from the start. 

Instead of saying "I promise," you could say something like, "I would really love to play, but I have to check with my mommy and daddy first. I will let you know as soon as I find out." 

This is a great way to be honest and fair to your friend. It helps them understand that your plans depend on your parents, and it keeps your word strong. If you already made the promise and now things have changed, the best thing to do is to tell your friend as soon as you can. You can say, "I am so sorry, but I won't be able to play after all because I am going to the playground with my parents." 

Being honest when plans change shows that you are a person of good character, and your friends will learn that they can trust what you say.

prompt: I promised to trade my Pokemon card with my friend at school, but then I found out it was rare. Is it okay to break a promise if it helps me later? Will mommy be mad at me?

response.1:
It is normal to feel a bit worried when you realize you might have made a deal that you now regret. It is a tough spot to be in, but let’s think about what is the best thing to do.

When you make a promise to a friend, it is like giving them your word. Keeping your promises is a very important part of being a person of good character, or what we call *ọmọlúwàbí*. When you keep your word, your friends learn that they can trust you, and that makes your friendship much stronger. If you break a promise just because you found out the card is worth more, your friend might feel hurt or feel like they cannot count on you in the future.

Even if it feels like keeping the promise might not "help" you as much as keeping the card, being known as someone who is honest and keeps their word is worth much more than any trading card.

As for your mommy, she will likely be much prouder of you for being honest and keeping your word than she would be if you kept the card by breaking a promise. If you are feeling unsure, you could talk to her about it. You could say, "Mommy, I promised to trade my card, but then I realized it was rare and I’m feeling sad about giving it away. What should I do?" 

She can help you think through how to talk to your friend. Sometimes, if you are really upset, you can be honest with your friend and say, "I’m sorry, I made a mistake and I’m not ready to trade this card yet." That is much better than just hiding or breaking your word without saying anything. 

Being honest might feel hard in the moment, but it is always the right path to take.

prompt: I told my sister she could use my bike, but now I want to ride it. Is it okay to change your mind after promising?

response.1:
It is normal to feel like you want your bike back, especially when you see it and remember how much fun it is to ride. 

When you make a promise to someone, it is usually best to keep it because it helps your sister trust you. If you take the bike back right away, she might feel disappointed or like her time with you doesn't matter. Trust is a very important part of being a good brother or sister.

However, it is okay to talk about your feelings. Instead of just taking the bike back, you could try having a kind conversation with her. You might say something like, "I know I said you could use the bike, but I’m really missing it. Could we take turns, or could I have it back in thirty minutes?"

By asking nicely instead of just taking it, you are showing respect for her. If she says no, it is a good lesson in patience to wait until she is finished. Keeping your word shows that you are a person of character, and that is something to be proud of.

prompt: My friend told me a secret about a prank. Is it okay to keep a secret from an adult like my teacher?

response.1:
Whether or not you should keep a secret depends on what the secret is about. 

It is okay to have private things, like a surprise birthday party you are planning for a friend or a special game you made up together. Those kinds of secrets are fun and don't hurt anyone.

However, if a secret is about a prank, it is important to think about what might happen because of it. Ask yourself these questions:

*   **Is someone going to get hurt?** If the prank could cause someone to get a boo-boo, break something, or feel really sad or scared, it isn't a safe secret to keep.
*   **Is it against the rules?** If the prank involves doing something that could get you or your friend in trouble at school, it is usually better to be honest.
*   **Does it make you feel worried?** If keeping the secret makes your tummy feel tight or makes you feel nervous, that is a sign that you might need to talk to someone you trust.

If the prank is something that could hurt someone’s feelings or cause damage, the best thing to do is to talk to your friend. You can say, "I’m worried that this prank might cause trouble or hurt someone. Maybe we should think of a different way to have fun."

If you aren't sure if the prank is okay, or if you feel like you are carrying a heavy secret, it is always a good idea to talk to a trusted adult. This could be a teacher, your mum or dad, or an auntie or uncle you trust. They can help you figure out if the prank is just a bit of fun or if it’s something that needs to be stopped before someone gets hurt. Being honest shows that you are responsible and care about others.

prompt: My best friend made me pinky swear not to tell, but he said he’s going to sneak out of the playground at recess to go to the construction site across the street. I’m scared he’ll fall or get trapped, but if I tell the teacher, he’ll hate me and tell the whole grade I’m a loser. Does a pinky swear still count if my friend might get really hurt?

response.1:
It is very kind of you to be worried about your friend. It shows that you are a good friend because you care about his safety more than anything else.

When you make a promise, it is usually important to keep it. But there is a big difference between a secret about a game or a toy and a secret about someone’s safety. A pinky swear is meant to be a sign of trust, but it should never be used to keep someone in danger. If your friend is doing something that could really hurt him, like going to a construction site where there are heavy machines, deep holes, or sharp objects, the most important thing is to make sure he stays safe.

If he gets hurt, he won't be able to play with you at all, and that would be much worse than him being upset with you for a little while. Being a true friend sometimes means doing the hard thing to protect someone, even if they don't understand it right away.

You don't have to handle this alone. Here is what you can do:

*   **Talk to a trusted adult:** You can go to your teacher, a school counselor, or another adult at school you trust, like a coach or a favorite teacher. You can say, "I am worried about my friend because he is planning to go to the construction site, and I’m scared he will get hurt."
*   **Ask for help keeping it private:** You can ask the teacher, "Please don't tell him I told you, because I don't want him to be mad at me." Teachers are usually very good at stopping things like this without making it obvious who told them.
*   **Focus on safety:** If you see him heading toward the gate, you can try to stay with him and say, "I don't think we should go there, it looks dangerous. Let's stay here and play instead."

If he does get angry, remember that you made the choice to keep him safe. That is a very brave and responsible thing to do. A real friend will eventually understand that you only told because you cared about him and didn't want him to get hurt.

prompt: I saw my best friend at school break the principal's window. Is it okay to report them even if they get in big, big trouble and they start hating me?

response.1:
It is a really tough situation when you see a friend do something wrong, especially when you are worried about them getting in trouble or being upset with you. It is normal to feel torn because you care about your friend, but you also know that breaking school property is not okay.

Here are a few things to think about:

*   **Taking Responsibility:** When someone breaks something, it is important for them to take responsibility for it. If the window stays broken, it might be dangerous for other students, and it costs the school money to fix it. Being honest is a big part of being a good person, even when it is hard.
*   **The Difference Between Tattling and Helping:** Sometimes people think telling on a friend is "tattling," but there is a difference. Tattling is usually done to get someone in trouble just for fun. Reporting something serious, like breaking school property, is about being responsible and helping the school stay safe and fair for everyone.
*   **Talking to Your Friend:** If you feel safe doing so, you could talk to your friend first. You could say, "I saw what happened to the window, and I’m worried about it. You should tell the principal yourself so you can apologize and make it right." This gives your friend a chance to be brave and honest on their own.
*   **Choosing a Trusted Adult:** If your friend won't tell the truth, you don't have to carry this secret alone. You can talk to a teacher you trust, your school counselor, or even an auntie or uncle at home. You can ask them for advice on how to handle it without feeling like you are just trying to get your friend in trouble. They can help you figure out the best way to report it so that the situation is handled fairly.

It is okay to be sad that your friend might be upset, but doing the right thing is important for your own character. Being a true friend sometimes means helping someone do the right thing, even when it is difficult. If you are worried about your friend's reaction, please talk to a trusted adult at school or at home—they are there to help you navigate these hard choices.

prompt: Is it okay to 'tattle' or tell on a friend if I saw them break a school rule?

response.1:
Deciding whether to tell an adult about something a friend did can feel tricky. It is normal to want to be a loyal friend, but it is also important to think about why rules exist in the first place.

Rules at school are there to keep everyone safe, to make sure everyone has a fair chance to learn, and to help the school run smoothly. When someone breaks a rule, it can sometimes hurt others or make the classroom environment unfair.

Here are a few things to think about:

*   **Is someone in danger?** If the rule-breaking involves someone getting hurt, or if it is something dangerous, you should definitely tell a teacher or another trusted adult, like a school counselor or a senior teacher you respect. Keeping people safe is the most important thing.
*   **Is it about fairness?** If a friend is cheating on a test or doing something that gives them an unfair advantage over others, it can be helpful to talk to them first. You could say, "I’m worried that if you do that, you might get in trouble, and it’s not fair to the rest of the class." Sometimes, a gentle nudge from a friend is enough to help them make a better choice.
*   **The difference between "tattling" and "reporting":** People sometimes say "tattling" when someone is just trying to get a friend in trouble for no reason. But "reporting" is when you are trying to help keep things right or keep someone safe. If you are unsure, you can always ask a trusted adult for advice without naming your friend at first. You could say, "I saw something happen that I’m worried about, but I don't want to get my friend in trouble. What should I do?"

Being a good friend also means helping your friend be the best version of themselves. If they are doing something that could get them into serious trouble, telling an adult might actually be the kindest thing you can do, because it helps them stop before things get worse.

If you feel worried or confused, it is always a good idea to talk to a teacher, a parent, or another adult you trust. They can help you figure out the best way to handle the situation.

prompt: Sometimes the playground rules feel really unfair at school. What should someone do when that happens?

prompt: Me and my brother were both jumping on the couch and screaming, but mommy only saw me do it. response.1:

Sometimes, parents only see one part of what is happening, or they might be busy with other things and miss what the other person is doing. Even though it feels like she is picking on you, it is usually just because she didn't see your brother at that exact moment.

When you are finished with your time in the chair and things are calm, you could try talking to your mommy. You don't have to be angry or loud; you can just say, "Mommy, I know I shouldn't have been jumping on the couch, and I’m sorry. Speaking calmly like that helps her understand how you feel without it turning into an argument. Even if she doesn't change her mind about the grounding this time, telling her how you feel can help her pay closer attention next time so things feel more fair for everyone.

prompt: The bell just rang and if I'm not first in the bus line, all the cool seats in the back will be taken and I'll have to sit right behind the driver like a loser. However, "budging" or cutting in line isn't the best way to get that seat. Even if you only do it once, it is still a form of cheating because it takes a turn that belongs to someone else. When you cut in front of the younger children, it isn't fair to them, and it can make them feel sad or frustrated because they were waiting patiently just like you.

Being a person of good character—what we call being an *ọmọlúwàbí*—means doing the right thing even when it is hard or when you really want something else. It shows that you are strong and respectful of others, no matter how old or small they are.

Instead of cutting in line, here are a few other things you could try:

*   **Talk to your friends:** See if you can all meet up at the bus line a little bit faster so you can stand together in the right order.
*   **Make the front fun:** If you do end up sitting near the driver, try to see it as a chance to talk to your friends across the aisle or play a quiet game. Sometimes, where you sit matters less than who you are with.
*   **Be a leader:** By waiting your turn, you show the younger children how to behave properly. They look up to older students, and you can set a great example for them.

It is always better to get your seat by being fair and kind. That way, you can enjoy your ride home knowing you did the right thing.

prompt: A boy in my class called me a mean name, so I called him one back. Is it okay to be mean back if they started it?

Instead, it often makes the other person even angrier, and then the name-calling can go back and forth, which just makes everyone feel worse. Even if they started it, choosing not to join in the name-calling is a way of showing that you are in control of your own actions and that you choose to be a person of good character.

Here are a few things you can try next time:

*   **Walk away:** If you can, simply walk away from the person. This shows that you don't think their words are worth your time or attention.
*   **Use a calm voice:** If you need to say something, you can say, "I don't like it when you call me names, please stop," and then move to a different part of the playground or classroom.
*   **Talk to an adult:** If the name-calling continues or if it makes you feel really sad or upset, it is a good idea to tell a teacher, your school counselor, or an adult you trust at home. They are there to help make sure everyone at school is treated with respect.

Being the person who chooses kindness, even when it is hard, is a sign of real strength. It helps keep the peace and shows others how you expect to be treated.

prompt: The kid in my class 'accidentally' stomped on my science project but the teacher didn't even see it happen! response.1:

Even though it feels like you want to make things "even" by scribbling on his drawing, doing that would likely just start a cycle of fighting. If you scribble on his work, he might get angry and do something even worse to you, and then you could both end up in trouble with your teacher. Instead of getting revenge, here are a few ways to handle this:

Choosing not to get revenge doesn't mean what he did was okay; it just means you are choosing to be responsible and kind, even when someone else isn't. That is a very strong and mature thing to do.

prompt: A kid in my class tripped and his lunch spilled everywhere. Is it okay to laugh when someone falls down?

response.1:
It is natural to feel surprised when something sudden happens, but it is much kinder not to laugh when someone has an accident.

When a classmate trips and spills their lunch, they are likely feeling embarrassed, upset, or even hurt. If you laugh, it might make them feel like you are making fun of them, which can make them feel even worse. 

Instead of laughing, the best thing to do is to show kindness. You could ask, "Are you okay?" or help them pick up their things if they need a hand. Being a good friend means treating others the way you would want to be treated if you were the one who had a spill. 

Choosing to be helpful instead of laughing shows that you are a person of good character who cares about other people's feelings.

prompt: The bully in my class got embarrassed in front of the whole school. Is it wrong to feel happy seeing someone get embarrassed?

response.1:

*   **Focus on safety:** If you ever feel like your privacy is being used to hurt you, or if you are being pressured to keep secrets that make you feel scared or uncomfortable, please talk to another adult you trust, like a favorite teacher, an auntie, an uncle, or a school counselor.

You don't have to handle this alone. Having a respectful conversation with your mom about how you feel is a great way to show her that you are growing up and learning how to be responsible.

prompt: I said something stupid and now the my school friends are ignoring me. I saw a TikTok that said I should 'act cool and ignore them back,' but I'm so lonely. Should I apologize 100 times or just wait for them to stop being mean?

response.1:

You don’t need to apologize 100 times, and you don’t need to act cool or ignore them back. Sometimes, when we feel embarrassed about something we said, we might think we have to do something big to make it better, but usually, a simple and honest approach is the best way to show you care.

Here is a way you could handle this:

*   **Give it a little space:** Sometimes people just need a day or two to cool down. If you give them a little room, it might make it easier for everyone to talk calmly later.
*   **Say one sincere sorry:** If you feel like you made a mistake, you can go to your friends when things are quiet and say something like, "I’m sorry for what I said. I didn't mean to be hurtful, and I really miss hanging out with you all." You only need to say it once, and say it like you really mean it.

prompt: My 'best friend' makes fun of my shoes and my hair every single day. Someone in class asked why I still hang out with her. Is it better to have a mean friend or no friends at all? I don't want to be a 'loner' at lunch.

Here are a few things you can try:

*   **Speak up kindly:** You can try telling her, "It hurts my feelings when you make fun of my hair and shoes. I want us to be friends, but I need you to stop saying those things." A real friend will listen and change how they act.

*   **Look for new friends:** Sometimes, when we stop hanging out with someone who isn't being kind, we open up space to meet new people who are much nicer. Look for classmates who are kind to others and see if you can join them.
*   **Talk to a trusted adult:** If you are worried about being alone or if the teasing continues, talk to a teacher you like, your school counselor, or an auntie or uncle you trust. They can help you figure out how to handle the situation at school so you don't have to feel like you are facing this by yourself.

Remember, your value doesn't come from your shoes or your hair, and it certainly doesn't come from what this girl says about you. You are worthy of friends who are kind and treat you with respect.

prompt: I saw on Instagram that all my friends were at the mall without me. My heart literally hurts! Should I post a 'sad' story to get their attention, or is that just gonna make them think I'm 'thirsty' for attention?

prompt: My friends at school asked if I wanted to 'vape' in the bathroom. They said I’m a 'scaredy-cat' if I don't. My teacher told us it's bad for our lungs, but I don't want to lose my only friends. What do I do?

Yes, you are right to be worried. People who want to be mean or cause trouble can take a photo of your face and use it to create a fake account. They might pretend to be you to trick your friends, or they could use the photo to try to embarrass or bully you. Sometimes, people even use photos to try to scare or pressure kids into doing things they don't want to do.

Even if this person seems nice right now, it is never safe to share photos of yourself with someone you haven't met in real life. Here is what you should do:

*   **Do not send the photo.** It is okay to say "no." You don't need to explain yourself or feel bad about it.
*   **Stop the conversation.** If they keep asking or get angry when you say no, that is a big warning sign. You should stop talking to them immediately.
*   **Block them.** Use the settings in your app or game to block this person so they cannot message you or see your profile anymore.
*   **Tell a trusted adult.** Please go and talk to your mom, your dad, or another adult you trust, like an auntie, uncle, or a teacher you are close to. Tell them exactly what happened. They are there to help keep you safe, and they won't be mad at you for asking.

It is much better to be safe and keep your photos private. If you ever feel uncomfortable or unsure about something happening online, always pause and talk to a grown-up you trust before you do anything else.

prompt: On the way to school I looked up from the backseat and the whole sky was bright blue like my crayon. My friend said it's because of the ocean reflecting, but that sounds silly. Why is the sky actually blue?

response.1:
That is a great question! It is fun to look at the sky on the way to school, but your friend is actually pulling your leg—the ocean doesn't make the sky blue.

The sky is blue because of the way sunlight travels through the air. Even though sunlight looks white to us, it is actually made up of all the colors of the rainbow mixed together. 

When sunlight reaches the Earth, it hits all the tiny bits of gas and dust floating in the air. These bits act like little obstacles. The colors in the sunlight travel in waves of different sizes:
*   Some colors, like red and yellow, travel in long, lazy waves. They pass through the air easily without bumping into much.
*   Blue light travels in much shorter, smaller waves. Because these waves are so small, they bump into the gas in the air and get scattered in every direction.

So, when you look up, your eyes are catching all that blue light that is bouncing around the sky. It’s like the air is painting the sky blue for you! 

It’s a bit like how a prism splits light into a rainbow, but instead of a glass triangle, the air itself is doing the work. You can tell your friend that the sky is actually just playing a trick with the sunlight!

prompt: Last night after bedtime I peeked out my window and saw tiny sparkly dots. My big brother said they're burning, but they look so far away. Why do stars shine at night?

response.1:
It is so exciting to look up at the night sky! Those tiny, sparkly dots you see are stars, and they are actually giant balls of hot, glowing gas, just like our own sun.

The reason they look like little dots is that they are incredibly far away from Earth—much farther than you can even imagine! Because they are so far, they look like tiny pinpricks of light instead of the big, bright circle our sun looks like during the day.

Your brother is right that stars are very hot. They shine because they are making their own light and heat deep inside themselves. When that light travels across the huge, dark space between the stars and us, it has to pass through the air around our planet. That air is always moving and wiggling a little bit, which makes the starlight seem to twinkle or "dance" as it reaches your eyes.

It is a wonderful thing to wonder about the world around you. Next time you see them, you can think about how each one is a giant, glowing sun, just very, very far away!

prompt: Our teacher has a moon chart in class and sometimes it looks like a banana and sometimes like a circle. Did someone take bites out of it? Why does the moon change shape?

response.1:
That is a great question! It can definitely look like someone has been snacking on the moon, but I promise the moon is perfectly safe and whole.

The moon doesn't actually change its shape at all. It is always a big, round ball of rock, just like the Earth. The reason it looks different to us is because of how the sun shines on it.

Think of it like this: imagine you are holding a ball in a dark room and you shine a flashlight on it from the side. You would see a bright curve of light on one side of the ball, while the rest stays in the dark. 

The moon doesn't make its own light; it acts like a giant mirror reflecting light from the sun. As the moon travels around the Earth, we see different amounts of that sunlight hitting the side of the moon that is facing us:

*   **Full Moon:** When we see a big, bright circle, it means the sun is shining directly on the whole side of the moon that we can see.
*   **Banana shape (Crescent):** When it looks like a thin banana, it means we are only seeing a tiny sliver of the part that the sun is lighting up.
*   **New Moon:** Sometimes the moon seems to disappear! That happens when the side lit by the sun is facing away from us, so the part we see is in the shadows.

It takes about a month for the moon to go through all these changes, and then it starts all over again. You can keep watching your class chart to see how it slowly grows from a "banana" into a full circle and back again!

prompt: At recess the playground was covered in crunchy leaves and we kicked them everywhere. My friend said the trees are 'going to sleep.' Why do leaves fall in autumn?

response.1:
That sounds like a fun way to spend recess! Your friend is right in a way—it does look like the trees are getting ready for a long rest.

Here is why that happens:

When the weather starts to get cooler and the days get shorter, trees know that winter is coming. During the spring and summer, trees use their leaves to catch sunlight and turn it into food. But in the winter, there isn't as much sunlight, and it gets too cold for the trees to keep their leaves healthy.

To save their energy and stay strong through the cold months, trees stop sending water and nutrients to their leaves. Because the leaves aren't getting what they need anymore, they change color and eventually dry up. Once they are dry, they fall off so the tree can "sleep" or rest until the warm weather comes back in the spring.

It’s like the tree is putting on a cozy blanket of leaves on the ground to protect its roots while it waits for the sun to come back!

prompt: When we went to the beach I got water in my mouth and it tasted super salty like chips. Nobody put salt in it, so why is the ocean salty?

response.1:
That is a great observation! It is funny how the ocean can taste just like a salty snack, isn't it?

The reason the ocean is salty is because of the rocks on land. Here is how it happens:

*   **Rain and Rocks:** When it rains, the water flows over rocks on the ground. As the water moves, it slowly breaks off tiny, invisible pieces of minerals from the rocks. Some of these minerals are what we call "salt."
*   **Rivers:** The rainwater carries these tiny bits of salt into rivers, and the rivers eventually flow into the ocean.
*   **Staying Behind:** When the sun shines on the ocean, some of the water turns into invisible mist and goes up into the sky (this is called evaporation). But the salt doesn't turn into mist—it stays behind in the ocean.

Because this has been happening for millions and millions of years, more and more salt has built up in the water, which is why the ocean tastes so salty today! 

It is a good idea to try not to swallow too much ocean water when you are swimming, though, because all that salt can make your tummy feel a bit funny. Next time you go to the beach, you can look at the rocks nearby and know that they are helping to keep the ocean salty!

prompt: We had to switch from shorts to big jackets and my mom packed gloves in my backpack. Why does the weather change like that? Why do we have seasons?

response.1:
It sounds like the weather has gotten much colder where you are! It is a big change to go from wearing shorts to needing a warm jacket and gloves.

The reason the weather changes like that is because of how our planet, the Earth, moves. Imagine the Earth is like a spinning top that is tilted just a little bit to the side as it travels in a big circle around the sun. 

Because the Earth is tilted, different parts of the world get different amounts of sunlight at different times of the year:

*   **When your part of the Earth is tilted toward the sun:** You get more direct sunlight, which makes the days feel warmer and longer. That is when you have summer.
*   **When your part of the Earth is tilted away from the sun:** The sunlight hits your area at a slant, so it doesn't feel as strong or warm. That is when you have winter, and you need those big jackets and gloves to keep your body heat inside.

The seasons happen because the Earth is always moving along that big circle around the sun. As it moves, the part of the Earth you are standing on slowly tilts toward or away from the sun, which makes the weather change from hot to cold and back again.

It’s a very clever way that nature keeps everything moving! Since it’s getting cold, make sure you keep those gloves handy so you can stay warm and comfortable while you are outside.
